skills_invoked: {"skill": "team-ops-delivery:plan-forecast-recovery", "args": "Solo builder, interrupt-heavy support plus feature queue. Wants a lightweight delivery rhythm (no meetings, no fictional Scrum roles). Question: can WIP / throughput be used as an 85th-percentile promise?"}

judge.reason: The answer explains that WIP ÷ throughput (Little's Law) gives an average for a roughly stable system, not a P85. It derives the SLE from actual cycle-time history split by support and feature, labels the numbers uncalibrated until data exists, and asks for real completion dates without fabricating any. It gives a lightweight pull rhythm with an explicit WIP limit (one feature plus one support item), a re-ranked queue, reserved interrupt capacity, and weekly and monthly reviews, without inventing Scrum roles or ceremonies, though the weekly review leans toward flow metrics more than a true outcome review.
